content.overview: This lesson supports practitioners to identify when available information may meet a mandatory-reporting threshold and to route that concern into the correct human-led reporting workflow. It focuses on threshold awareness, time sensitivity, and documentation that shows why review or reporting was triggered.
learning_outcomes: Recognise the indicators that may trigger mandatory-reporting review in child-safety contexts
Distinguish threshold detection from the act of filing or approving a report
Document the concern, evidence basis, and urgency in a way that supports lawful escalation
Use role authority and human approval checkpoints before any external report is sent
key_concepts: A trigger identifies that reporting review may be required; it does not replace authorised human action
Thresholds depend on jurisdiction, role, policy, and the facts currently available
Incomplete information should not block urgent review when immediate safety concerns are present
The audit trail must show what concern was detected, who reviewed it, and what action followed
practice_activities: Review a scenario and identify the information that may meet a reporting threshold
Draft a concise escalation note that records concern, source, urgency, and next reviewer
Map the internal approval steps that must occur before any external notification is made
Identify what additional facts would strengthen the record without delaying necessary review
facilitator_notes: Be explicit that no automated workflow should contact an external agency on its own
Encourage participants to separate policy thresholds from personal comfort levels
Use examples that show why timely escalation matters even when information is still developing
Reinforce the need for jurisdiction-specific supervision and legal/policy guidance
reflection_prompts: What signs make me most uncertain about a reporting threshold?
How do I avoid both delay and overreach when concerns are serious?
What internal pathway should be fastest and clearest in my workplace?
How would I show that I acted responsibly if my decision were later reviewed?
content.printable_summary:
Mandatory-Reporting Trigger — Key Takeaways:
- Detect potential reporting thresholds early.
- Treat the trigger as a review signal, not an automated report.
- Document concern, source, urgency, and reviewer path.
- Keep authorised humans responsible for external action.
